I am 49 years old, and I have farmed our family’s land in Quzhou since I left primary school. I hold about 7 mu of flat, irrigated fields near the village. Around here, the land does not rest — we do wheat and corn double-cropping because that is what the climate and the market allow. My wheat is already in the ground; I sowed it last October after rotary tillage, using an improved variety like the ones my neighbors and I have relied on for years. Now that spring has arrived, the wheat is reviving and I have already top-dressed urea once. I will irrigate three times in total — green-up, jointing, and grain-filling — and spray three times for weeds, aphids, and disease. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will not waste a single day. I will plant hybrid corn seed right into the stubble with no-tillage, just like most of us do now to save time and fuel before the summer rains arrive. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress more nitrogen when the corn is knee-high. Corn needs two good irrigations — one at jointing and one at silking — and I will spray twice for corn borers and weeds. If all goes well, I should get about 550 kg per mu. I do not grow cotton or other crops; the wheat-corn rotation is steady, and the grain buyers come right to the village. That is what I know, and that is what feeds my family.
